text: dsh-bilibili-pro 是面向 DSH 的 Bilibili 视频分析插件，通过注册分析技能和工具，让 agent 从视频链接读取资料并整理内容。它可获取视频信息与 AI/CC 字幕，按页读取或搜索长转录文本；没有字幕时可调用 Bcut 语音转写，并按指定时刻或场景变化截取画面。截图可选交给配置的视觉模型描述，技能可据此产出带时间线的 HTML 报告。适合整理 B 站课程、访谈和演示视频；登录与视觉服务按需配置。

dsh-bilibili-pro is a DSH plugin for analyzing Bilibili videos. Its skill and tools retrieve video details and subtitles, browse or search transcripts, transcribe audio, and capture selected frames. Optional vision descriptions and an HTML timeline report are also available.
想把 B 站视频内容整理成带时间线的笔记。
帮我提取一个 Bilibili 视频的字幕并搜索其中的关键词。
I want to summarize a Bilibili video and inspect its transcript in manageable sections.
dsh-bilibili-pro 的功能「字幕检索」：提取并校验视频字幕，支持多种格式；长文本可分段读取或搜索关键词。通过字幕、转录分页和搜索工具触发。
dsh-bilibili-pro 的功能「转写与画面采集」：可用 Bcut 转写无字幕视频，并按时刻或场景截取画面；配置视觉服务后可生成画面描述。通过 bilibili_transcribe 和 bilibili_frames 工具触发。
dsh-bilibili-pro 使用前须知：插件会向 Bilibili 服务请求视频信息、字幕或转写所需音频；画面描述仅在配置视觉服务时发送截图到所选端点。
dsh-bilibili-pro 使用前须知：读取 AI 字幕可需 Bilibili 登录；扫码所得 cookie 保存在本机 DSH 配置目录，也可提供 SESSDATA。视觉服务的 bearer key 为可选配置。

dsh-bilibili-pro README · dsh-bilibili-pro：> dsh-bilibili-pro 0.2.3: validated AI/CC subtitles with a lossless, disk-backed
> transcript pagination layer (`parts`, cursor, time index, gaps) plus keyword
> search, picture-driven frame capture with optional vision descriptions, and a
> no-subtitle ASR chain: **Bcut (必剪) first**, with an **optional** on-demand
> faster-whisper fallback. No faster-whisper package, virtualenv or model is

dsh-bilibili-pro README · dsh-bilibili-pro：Bilibili video understanding for DeepSeek Harness: sign in once by QR code, pull a video's **AI/CC subtitle track**, and summarize it into a **self-contained HTML report**. When a video has no subtitle track, the plugin transcribes it with Bilibili's own Bcut ASR (no local model); if Bcut cannot handle the audio, an optional faster-whisper runtime can be installed on demand, persistently or just for one video.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · dsh-bilibili-pro：Bilibili hides AI subtitles from signed-out clients, so the plugin signs in through the official passport QR flow and stores the cookie jar locally. The login code is rendered by the plugin itself and never sent to a third-party image service.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · What it adds：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bilibili_subtitles` | Extract the AI/CC subtitle track as a timestamped transcript; validates before returning, supports bilingual merge, and renders Markdown, text, SRT, ASS, LRC, or JSON |
| `bilibili_transcript_part` | Read one bounded part of the saved transcript by `part` or `cursor` (no re-fetch); `max_chars` repacks at another size and the returned cursor carries that packing |
| `bilibili_transcript_search` | Literal keyword search over the saved transcript, returning the time, part number, and surrounding context of each hit |
| `bilibili_video_info` | Metadata (title, UP, duration, description, stats, parts), the subtitle tracks the platform lists, Bilibili's own AI summary, and — when a video has no track — the comment section's long, well-liked "课代表" comments as a fallback source |
| `bilibili_transcribe` | No-subtitle fallback: Bcut (必剪) ASR first — no local model, no sign-in, lowest-bitrate audio candidate. `provider: auto` falls back to an already-installed faster-whisper runtime; with none installed it returns `status: "needs_asr_runtime"` instead of writing an empty bundle |
| `bilibili_asr_

dsh-bilibili-pro README · What it adds：*A real report: info card, one-line summary, key points, and a clickable timeline that jumps back into the player.*

Plus the `bilibili-video-analysis` skill, which turns a transcript into a Chinese HTML report using a bundled template (info card → one-line summary → key points → clickable timeline → glossary → **background annotations** → quotes → action list → collapsible full script).

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Install：This package is not published to npm. Install it from the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Rx12453345/dsh-bilibili-pro.git
cd dsh-bilibili-pro
npm install
mkdir -p dist

Keep `dist/` after installing: the profile records the tarball path.

On the desktop app, **Settings → Plugins → install from a local tarball** can be used instead of the CLI command. Keep FFmpeg on `PATH` for frame capture and local audio conversion.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Sign in：Ask the agent to summarize a Bilibili link; when the subtitle call reports that it is not signed in, it runs:

```
bilibili_login { action: "start" }   # returns a QR PNG path to show you
bilibili_login { action: "poll" }    # waits for the scan, saves the cookies
```

Scan with the Bilibili mobile app (「我的」→「扫一扫」). The cookies land in `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-cookies.json` (mode `0600`). Alternatively, skip the QR flow and put a session cookie in `$DSH_HOME/.env`:

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Sign in：```
BILIBILI_SESSDATA=your_sessdata_value
```

`bilibili_login { action: "status" }` reports which account is stored; `{ action: "logout" }` deletes the file.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · How the subtitles are actually fetched：The obvious-looking route is the wrong one. `x/player/v2` still carries a `subtitle.subtitles` field, but under load it answers with an unrelated or truncated body — summarizing it silently would put someone else's words in your report.

The route the web player itself uses is `x/v2/subtitle/web/view`, which answers in **protobuf**, and the paths it returns are **not fetchable as-is**:
section: How the subtitles are actually fetched

text:
dsh-bilibili-pro README · How the subtitles are actually fetched：1. `x/web-interface/view` maps the BV id to `aid`/`cid`.
2. `x/v2/subtitle/web/view?oid=<cid>&pid=<aid>&type=1&…`, WBI-signed, returns protobuf. The plugin walks the wire format directly (no generated schema, so new fields do not break it) and pulls out `lan`, `lan_doc`, and `subtitle_url`.
3. Each `//subtitle.bilibili.com/<path>` is XOR-decoded and rewritten to `//aisubtitle.hdslb.com/<path>?auth_key=…`, exactly as the player's own `F`/`U` helpers do. Those two key pairs are transcribed from `bfs/static/player/main/core.*.js`, and a unit test pins the transform so a wrong character cannot slip through again.
4. The resulting JSON's `body[]` becomes the transcript.
section: How the subtitles are actually fetched

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · How the subtitles are actually fetched：Because the service can still answer with a short body under rate limiting, `bilibili_subtitles` validates before returning and retries with growing backoff, re-requesting the track each time.
section: How the subtitles are actually fetched

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · What "validated" means：Coverage alone cannot tell a real transcript from a convincing fake — the legacy route returned a complete, correctly sized transcript of a *different* video. The plugin therefore scores three signals and reports a verdict:

dsh-bilibili-pro README · What "validated" means：| Verdict | Condition | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strong` | a title keyword appears in the transcript and coverage ≥ 50 % | use it |
| `weak` | coverage ≥ 70 % but no title keyword matched (common with clickbait titles or an English title over Chinese speech) | use it, but say the match is weak |
| `fail` | too few segments, coverage < 50 %, or coverage > 200 % (a transcript longer than the video is someone else's) | refuse it and fall back |

dsh-bilibili-pro README · What "validated" means：Keyword matching covers CJK fragments (2–4 characters) and Latin tokens (3+ characters, stop-words removed), so `implement-spec`, `React`, or `海绵宝宝` all count.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Fallback chain：1. `bilibili_subtitles` — the real track.
2. `bilibili_video_info` — Bilibili's own AI summary, plus the video description.
3. `bilibili_video_info` with `comments` — long (≥ 200 chars), well-liked (≥ 3) comments; the "课代表" summary a viewer wrote by hand. Fetched automatically when the video has no track at all.
4. `bilibili_transcribe` — Bcut (必剪) ASR: anonymous, model-free, and the default for no-subtitle videos. Bcut accepts only roughly 10 minutes of audio, so a longer no-subtitle video is rejected (poll state 3).
5. Optional local fallback: if Bcut fails, `bilibili_transcribe` reuses an already-installed faster-whisper runtime. With none installed it returns `status: "needs_asr_runtime"` with the two install choices below — it never downloads on its own.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Fallback chain：Human-uploaded (CC) tracks are preferred over machine-generated ones for the same language, and every step that used a fallback marks the source in the report.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Bilingual tracks and formats：`bilibili_subtitles` can merge a second track under each line — the way bilingual subtitle tools work:

```
bilibili_subtitles({ url: "BV1TXHY6aETi", lang: "ai-zh", bilingual: "ai-en", format: "srt", out: "bilingual.srt" })
```

Output formats: `markdown`, `text`, `srt`, `ass`, `lrc`, `json`.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Background annotations in the report：A transcript is full of names that mean nothing without context. The skill requires the report to annotate them: people and teams, products and libraries, organisations, jargon and abbreviations, and the events being referenced. Each note is one or two sentences — what it is, and why the video mentions it — with a source link whenever the fact came from a web search, and an explicit `（未能核实）` when it could not be confirmed. Each marker shows the note **on hover** (a CSS-only popup, so it works offline and in any viewer), and clicking the number jumps to the full list at the end for reading straight through or printing. The popup and the appendix are generated from the same text, so they cannot drift apart.

section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper：Bcut rejects audio longer than roughly 10 minutes. For those videos the assistant can offer an **optional** faster-whisper fallback, with two explicit choices:
section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text:
dsh-bilibili-pro README · No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper：- **persistent** — `bilibili_asr_setup { action: "install", mode: "persistent" }` creates `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-asr/{venv,models}`; the venv and downloaded model are kept and reused by every later video.
- **temporary** — `bilibili_asr_setup { action: "install", mode: "temporary", out_dir: "..." }` creates `<out_dir>/.asr-runtime`; after the transcript bundle is written the venv and model are deleted. A temp state file under `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-asr` lets a later call find it even from another `out_dir`.
section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper：Neither mode is ever started automatically. If Bcut fails and no runtime exists, `bilibili_transcribe` returns `status: "needs_asr_runtime"` with `bcut_error`, both options, and an estimated model size instead of writing an empty bundle. `install` creates the virtualenv and pip-installs faster-whisper but **does not download the model**; the first local transcription does (`small` ≈ 500 MB, `medium` ≈ 1.5 GB). The plugin bundles no faster-whisper package, venv, or model — GitHub "install and use" still means Bcut works immediately, and faster-whisper is an opt-in extra. Point `asrPython` at an existing interpreter with faster-whisper to skip the install entirely; `bilibili_asr_setup { action: "status" }` probes it and reports whether a runtime is already usable.
section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper：The installer pins PyAV below 19 (`faster-whisper` + `av<19`) for now: PyAV 19 removed the `av.open(..., metadata_errors=...)` argument that faster-whisper 1.2.1 still passes, so an unpinned install would fail as soon as the model opens the audio. When transcribing locally, the audio is downloaded by Node (with the Bilibili referer and a size cap) and converted by ffmpeg from that local file — not by ffmpeg opening the remote URL — because ffmpeg's own TLS stack may reject the local proxy CA.
section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text: dsh-bilibili-pro README · No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper：Real verification on a 9-minute no-subtitle video (`BV1hhHi65EnQ`): Bcut returned 159 utterances / 5,682 chars; the optional `faster-whisper` `small` model returned 103 segments / 5,464 chars in 107 seconds on CPU, with `source: "asr"` and the same paged bundle. Both results were readable through `bilibili_transcript_part` and `bilibili_transcript_search`. The model/venv are not shipped; they live only in the chosen runtime directory.
section: No-subtitle videos: Bcut, then optional faster-whisper

text:
dsh-bilibili-pro README · Configure：Every field is optional. Row config in a profile patch layer:

```yaml
- id: bilibili-pro
  name: 'dsh-bilibili-pro'
  config:
    cookieFile: ~/.dsh/bilibili-cookies.json

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Configure：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cookieFile` | `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-cookies.json` | Where the session is stored |
| `sessdata` | `''` | Explicit `SESSDATA`; overrides the file |
| `language` | `ai-zh` | Preferred subtitle track |
| `retries` | `6` | Subtitle attempts before giving up |
| `retryBaseDelayMs` | `8000` | First backoff; each attempt adds 3 s |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-request timeout |
| `ffmpegPath` | autodetect | ffmpeg binary for the optional local fallback |
| `bcutTimeoutMs` | `600000` | Overall Bcut polling budget |
| `bcutPollMs` | `5000` | Bcut result poll interval |
| `asrPython` | `''` | Existing Python with faster-whisper; skips the install |
| `asrVenv` | `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-asr/venv` | Persistent fallback virtualenv |
| `asrModel` | `small` | faster-whisper model for the optional fallback |
| `asrModelDir` | `$DSH_HOME/bilibili-asr/models` | Model cache |
| `asrLanguage` | `auto` | Spoken language for the optional fallback |

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Configure：`BILIBILI_SESSDATA` and `BILIBILI_COOKIE_FILE` in the environment or `$DSH_HOME/.env` work too. `BILIBILI_ASR_PYTHON` (or `PYTHON`) points the optional fallback at an interpreter without editing the config.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Usage：```
bilibili_video_info({ url: "https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1puH46qE5x/" })
bilibili_subtitles({ url: "BV1c3HL6qEyq", out: "bilibili/BV1c3HL6qEyq/transcript.md" })
bilibili_subtitles({ url: "BV1TXHY6aETi", lang: "ai-zh", bilingual: "ai-en", format: "srt", out: "bilibili/BV1TXHY6aETi/bilingual.srt" })
bilibili_transcribe({ url: "BV1puH46qE5x" })                         # Bcut, no local install

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Usage：`bilibili_subtitles` returns the video record, the chosen track, validation/coverage stats, the on-disk manifest, and one bounded `part` plus `next_cursor` by default; pass `legacy_full: true` for the old full `timeline`/`transcript`/`segments` shape. `bilibili_transcript_part` and `bilibili_transcript_search` read the saved bundle (following a repacked cursor restores its packing). `bilibili_transcribe` uses the same paged bundle, so the same part/search tools work on ASR results; its `source` is `asr` and `asr.provider` is `bcut` or `faster-whisper`.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Limitations：- Chinese-first: the default track is `ai-zh`; other languages work through `lang`.
- Bcut is a Bilibili service with a practical limit of roughly 10 minutes of audio; longer no-subtitle videos need the optional local fallback (or another source such as Bilibili's AI summary / comment section).
- The optional faster-whisper fallback is not bundled: it downloads a model on first local use, and transcription quality tracks the chosen model; `small` is a speed/accuracy compromise. Bcut output usually has no punctuation; faster-whisper adds punctuation but both can mis-hear homophones.
- Bilibili rate-limits aggressively; a failed extraction is usually temporary.
- Multi-part videos are summarized one part at a time through the `page` argument.

dsh-bilibili-pro README · Upstream and attribution：This is an **independent package**, not a GitHub fork of a single upstream repository.
It is derived from `dsh-bilibili-summary` 0.1.3, which lives inside the
[`Adamaik/dsh-zcode-plugins`](https://github.com/Adamaik/dsh-zcode-plugins) monorepo at
`packages/bilibili-summary`. It also draws design from

repository-level, so a standalone plugin cannot carry a “forked from a subdirectory” badge;
the lineage is recorded in [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
